_meta.method: Three oracles, recorded side by side wherever two of them apply to the same number.  (1) r()/e() from Stata's own command, including twoway__histogram_gen, the subroutine histogram.ado itself calls. (2) THE PLOTTED POINTS: each twoway plot is saved to a live-format .gph,  makes its sersets addressable and  +  loads the exact drawn numbers back into memory; for mband this reaches the DERIVED serset (type median_bands) the graph engine computes at draw time.  (3) THE RESOLVED COMMAND LINE histogram rewrites itself into, read out of the .gph header by the python block.  Every value carries the command that produced it in its "cmd" field.
_meta.precision: Numbers were written with Stata's %20.17g, so doubles round-trip. Values that originate in a serset were stored by the graph engine as floats and are only float-accurate; compare those with a relative tolerance of about 1e-6, not for equality.
_meta.sampling: Curves of at most 41 points (64 for mband) are stored whole. Longer curves are stored at the 11 evenly spaced indices listed in sample_index, together with the full n_points and the min/max of every series.

contradictions_with_section_07_plan.fpfit.bwidth_and_degree_are_documented_b: Section 07 notes at / that fpfit/fpfitci never read bwidth() or degree(), contradicting dash.sthlp:559-560.  Stata's answer is that dash.sthlp is wrong to document them: twoway fpfit REJECTS both (_rc=198, "option bwidth() not allowed" / "option degree() not allowed").  degree() is spelled estopts(degree(#)) and there is no bandwidth concept in fpfit at all.  The right fix is to report them as unsupported, not to honour them.
contradictions_with_section_07_plan.fpfit.grid_size: Section 07 asks for "one grid size" for fpfit/fpfitci.  Stata uses no grid at all: both evaluate at the distinct observed x values, so the number of points is data-dependent.  The property to reproduce is that fpfit and fpfitci agree with each other and cover the full observed x range -- not that they share a constant like 200 or 150.
contradictions_with_section_07_plan.function.range_default: Section 07 requires at  that map_function honour range() "defaulting to the x-axis range rather than [0,1]".  Stata documents AND plots range(0 1), and measurement here shows the default does not change when another plot is present: function/auto:bare and function/auto:with_scatter both span x in [0,1] on 300 points.  dash's current [0,1] is therefore CORRECT as a default; what is actually missing is only that range() is ignored when the user gives it.
contradictions_with_section_07_plan.kdensity.n_default: and  have DIFFERENT default grid sizes (min(N,50) vs 300).  dash draws a plot, so 300 is the relevant one; r(bwidth) and r(kernel) are shared by both.
contradictions_with_section_07_plan.lowess_vs_lpoly_bwidth: Section 07 treats bwidth() as one concept.  It is two: lowess's bwidth() is a FRACTION of the sample (default .8) and lpoly's is an ABSOLUTE half-width in x units.  A single clamped-to-[0.01,1.0] implementation cannot be right for both.
contradictions_with_section_07_plan.mband.documented_vs_actual: help twoway_mband documents max(10, round(10*log10(N))) bands by default, but the graph engine does not use it.  See mband_default_band_count for the measured values.

ci_bands.formula.band: tval = invttail(e(df_r), (100-level)/200) ; lower = xb - tval*stdp ; upper = xb + tval*stdp
ci_bands.formula.confirmed_by: section ci_rebuild rebuilds every band from regress + predict and is compared point for point against the serset twoway actually plotted
ci_bands.formula.grid: x_i = min + (i-1)*(max-min)/(n-1) for i = 1..n, with n() defaulting to 100 and min/max the observed range of x
ci_bands.formula.se: stdp (the SE of the prediction) is the default; stdf and stdr are the alternatives

histogram.y_axis.formula: density: height = count/(N*width) ; fraction: count/N ; percent: 100*count/N ; frequency: count
histogram.y_axis.source: ado/base/t/twoway__histogram_gen.ado line 49 (else-if-zero-options branch sets type=density) and lines 221-232

kdensity.bwidth.formula: w = min(sd, (p75-p25)/1.349) ; if w == 0 then w = sd ; bwidth = 0.9*w/N^0.2

kdensity.kernel.source: help twoway_kdensity line 115; confirmed by r(kernel)

lowess.other_defaults.grid: the smooth is returned at the observed x values, one per observation -- there is no separate grid
lowess.other_defaults.weighting: tricube weighting is used (option  turns it off)

lpoly.bwidth.default: a rule-of-thumb (ROT) selector computed from the data
lpoly.bwidth.evidence: lpoly y x, bwidth(5) returns r(bwidth) == 5 on every dataset, while x_range recorded beside it spans four orders of magnitude
lpoly.bwidth.semantics: ABSOLUTE half-width in the units of x, NOT a fraction of the x range

lpoly.degree.source: help twoway_lpoly line 112; confirmed by r(degree)

lpoly.kernel.source: help twoway_lpoly line 100; confirmed by r(kernel)

lpoly.n.note: r(ngrid) can come back SMALLER than n() when a narrow bwidth() leaves grid points with no data inside the kernel window; see the bwidth5 probes

mband.bands.measured_default: round(min(sqrt(N), 10*log10(N))) -- i.e. the histogram bin rule with round() where histogram uses int().  This reproduces the plotted cross medians on all 14 measured (N, bands) pairs (N = 25 .. 2,246), while the documented max(10, round(10*log10(N))) reproduces only 3 of 14.  See mband_default_band_count_rule_search for the scored candidates and every pair.  This is measured, not read out of any source file.
mband.bands.semantics: the x axis is divided into # EQUAL-WIDTH intervals, then the median of y and the median of x are taken within each interval; it is those cross medians that are plotted. Intervals containing no observation produce no point.
mband.bands.semantics_confirmed_by: bands(5) and bands(20) are reproduced point for point by hand from the raw data; see bands_reproduced_by on each mband entry

unverified.histogram.y_axis_bar_heights_under_twowa: Bar heights are taken from twoway__histogram_gen's generate() output, which is the same subroutine twoway histogram calls, and cross-checked against the serset min/max in the saved .gph.  The individual bar heights inside a drawn twoway histogram serset were not enumerated separately.
unverified.lpoly.rot_bandwidth_formula: The closed form of lpoly's default rule-of-thumb bandwidth was NOT derived here.  It is computed in compiled Mata (_lpoly_work, called from ado/base/l/lpoly.ado line 311) and is documented only in [R] lpoly Methods and formulas, which is not machine-readable from this script.  The fixture records MEASURED r(bwidth) on four datasets under "lpoly" with variant "default"; check an implementation against those four numbers or against the manual.  No formula is claimed.
unverified.mband.default_band_count_formula: The band count the graph engine uses by default is NOT readable from any .ado -- the engine computes it -- and it does NOT match the documented max(10, round(10*log10(N))).  What IS established here is measurement: for each of 14 (N, bands) pairs, the band count that reproduces the plotted cross medians exactly was found by scanning B = 2..60.  round(min(sqrt(N), 10*log10(N))) fits all 14 and the documented rule fits 3.  A formula that fits 14 points over two orders of magnitude in N is strong evidence, but it is still inference from measurement and is recorded as such: an implementation should be checked against the pairs in mband_default_band_count_rule_search, not only against the formula.
